explain.name: capability_individuals
explain.text:
Purpose
Cp measures the tolerance width relative to short-term variation; Cpk also accounts for off-center measurements. Pp/Ppk use overall variation and can differ from Cp/Cpk.

Required input
Test Item, Sample ID, numeric measurement, and consistent LSL and/or USL. Pooled analysis also needs a subgroup ID. Tester, operator and slot are kept separate. Two observations minimum; larger representative samples improve precision.

Formulas used
mean = sum(x_i)/N; σ_overall = √(sum((x_i - mean)²)/(N-1)) (sample SD, no c4 correction).
Individuals in supplied collection order: MR_i = |x_i - x_(i-1)|; MRbar = sum(MR_i)/(N-1); σ_within = MRbar/1.128. Moving range length = 2.
Cp = (USL-LSL)/(6 × σ_within); Cpk = min((USL-mean)/(3 × σ_within), (mean-LSL)/(3 × σ_within)).
Pp = (USL-LSL)/(6 × σ_overall); Ppk = min((USL-mean)/(3 × σ_overall), (mean-LSL)/(3 × σ_overall)). One-sided limits use the available side for Cpk/Ppk; Cp/Pp are N/A.

Variables
x_i: observation i; N: measurement count; g: subgroup; n_g: subgroup size; mean_g: subgroup mean; df: within degrees of freedom; SS: sum of squares; Sp: pooled SD; Gamma: gamma function; MR: moving range; sigma: estimated standard deviation; LSL/USL: lower/upper specification limits.

Calculation steps
1. Check identities, numeric values, units and limits. 2. Partition tester/operator/slot. 3. Calculate mean, min and max. 4. Calculate within sigma using the selected method above. 5. Calculate sample overall SD. 6. Calculate each defined index at full precision. 7. Apply the selected Cpk threshold. Round only for display.

Acceptance
PASS only when unrounded Cpk > 1.33; otherwise FAIL. Undefined Cpk gives N/A, never a fabricated pass.

Worked example
Individuals [1,2,3,4,5], LSL=0, USL=6: N=5, mean=3, min=1, max=5; MRbar=1; σ_within=1/1.128=0.886524823; σ_overall=√(10/4)=1.581138830; Cp=Cpk=1.128; Pp=Ppk=0.632455532.
Pooled example: subgroups [1,2,3], [4,5,6], [7,8,9], limits0..20: mean=5, SS_within=6, df=6; Sp=1; σ_within=1/c4(7) when unbiasing is on; σ_overall=√(60/8).

Assumptions and limitations
Normal-distribution capability assumes a stable, representative process and independent observations. Moving ranges depend on collection order. Repeated readings of the same part can overstate process capability unless subgrouping matches the study design. Zero sigma produces N/A indices. Missing/invalid values are never silently discarded. No automatic normality test, transformation, confidence interval or nonnormal capability model is provided. Results are statistical estimates subject to model, data quality and assumptions.

explain.name: grr_legacy_solaredge
explain.text:
Purpose
Estimate the variation of a measurement system from repeated measurements of identified samples. With one operator (or none mapped) the model is a balanced one-way random-effects ANOVA: repeatability only. When two or more Operators measured the same samples, a crossed two-way ANOVA (Sample ID x Operator) also estimates operator reproducibility and the Sample x Operator interaction, as Minitab's Gage R&R (Crossed) does.

Required input
Test Item, Sample ID, numeric measurement and Trial. Map Trial or explicitly assign repetition order. At least two samples and two repeats per sample, with equal repetition counts. Typical design: 10 samples x 3 repetitions (x 3 operators when crossed). In a crossed study every operator must measure every sample the same number of times. Two-sided LSL/USL required for %SV/Tol. Tester and slot combinations are always evaluated separately.

Formulas used
mean_i = sum_j(x_ij)/r; mean = sum_i mean_i/p.
SS_Part = r × sum_i(mean_i-mean)²; df_Part=p-1; MS_Part=SS_Part/df_Part.
SS_Error=sum_i sum_j(x_ij-mean_i)²; df_Error=p × (r-1); MS_Error=SS_Error/df_Error.
F=MS_Part/MS_Error; p-value=P(F_(df_Part,df_Error) ≥ F).
variance_GRR=MS_Error; variance_Part=max((MS_Part-MS_Error)/r,0); variance_Total=variance_GRR+variance_Part.
σ_GRR=√(variance_GRR); σ_Part=√(variance_Part); σ_Total=√(variance_Total).
StudyVar_GRR=6 × σ_GRR; %SV/Tol=100 × StudyVar_GRR/(USL-LSL); %StudyVar=100 × σ_GRR/σ_Total.
NDC_raw=1.41 × σ_Part/σ_GRR; NDC=max(1,floor(NDC_raw)). Zero denominator gives N/A.
Rbar=mean of sample ranges; σ_chart=Rbar/d2(r). R limits: max(0,Rbar-3 × d3(r) × σ_chart), Rbar+3 × d3(r) × σ_chart. Xbar limits: mean ± 3 × σ_chart/√(r). Chart sigma is separate from ANOVA σ_GRR; d2/d3 constants implemented for 2..8 repeats.
Crossed model (two or more Operators on the same samples): p samples, o operators, r repetitions. SS_Oper=p × r × sum_j(mean_j-mean)²; SS_Int=r × sum_ij(mean_ij-mean_i-mean_j+mean)²; SS_Error=sum_ijk(x_ijk-mean_ij)²; df = p-1, o-1, (p-1) × (o-1), p × o × (r-1).
The interaction (F=MS_Int/MS_Error) is removed when its p-value ≥ 0.05 (Minitab's alpha to remove). With interaction: var_Repeat=MS_Error; var_Int=max((MS_Int-MS_Error)/r,0); var_Oper=max((MS_Oper-MS_Int)/(p × r),0); var_Part=max((MS_Part-MS_Int)/(o × r),0). Without it: MS_Pooled=(SS_Int+SS_Error)/(df_Int+df_Error); var_Repeat=MS_Pooled; var_Oper=max((MS_Oper-MS_Pooled)/(p × r),0); var_Part=max((MS_Part-MS_Pooled)/(o × r),0).
var_Reprod=var_Oper+var_Int; variance_GRR=var_Repeat+var_Reprod; variance_Total=variance_GRR+var_Part. Study variation, %StudyVar, %SV/Tol and NDC then use this σ_GRR exactly as above.

Variables
i: sample index; j: repetition (or operator in the crossed model); k: repetition within an operator; p: distinct sample count; o: operator count; r: repetitions per sample (per operator when crossed); x_ij: measurement; mean_i: sample mean; SS: sum of squares; df: degrees of freedom; MS: mean square; F: ANOVA statistic; sigma: estimated SD; GRR: gage repeatability (and reproducibility when crossed) for this system; LSL/USL: specification limits; d2/d3: expected range and range SD constants for normal samples; floor: truncate toward zero for positive numbers.

Calculation steps
1. Validate identities, trials, completeness and balance (and that every operator measured every sample, when crossed). 2. Keep each tester/slot separate; operators of one tester/slot are analyzed together. 3. Calculate sample means and grand mean. 4. Calculate SS, df, MS and ANOVA F/p. 5. Derive variance components, clipping negative components to zero without pooling them into other terms. 6. Derive SDs, study variation and all three key metrics. 7. Apply only the configured acceptance metric to unrounded results; report any informational metric that would fail on its own. 8. Generate charts from these same observations.

Acceptance
Profile: SolarEdge. Decision metric: %SV/Tol. %SV/Tol < 10%: PASS; 10% through 30% inclusive: CONDITIONAL PASS; above 30%: FAIL. SolarEdge always uses %SV/Tol alone; %Study Var and NDC are informational and cannot override this decision. When the decision is PASS or CONDITIONAL PASS but an informational metric would fail on its own (NDC < 5, or %Study Var / %SV/Tol > 30%), the result is flagged for review; the decision itself is unchanged.

Worked example
Samples [1,2,3], [4,5,6], [7,8,9], LSL=0, USL=20: p=3, r=3, N=9, mean=5. SS_Part=54, df_Part=2, MS_Part=27; SS_Error=6, df_Error=6, MS_Error=1. F=27, p=0.001. variance_Part=26/3; σ_GRR=1; σ_Total=√(29/3); %StudyVar=32.163376. With the selected multiplier, StudyVar=6, %SV/Tol=30%. NDC_raw=1.41 × √(26/3)=4.150928; NDC=4.

Assumptions and limitations
Independent normal repeatability errors with common variance; samples represent the intended part variation. Balanced repeated measurements only; unbalanced designs are rejected. With a single operator, reproducibility is not estimated, so the result describes repeatability only. Operator is the crossed factor and is treated as a random sample of its levels (a nest can stand in for the operator in a crossed study when the fixture is evaluated as a whole). To evaluate and approve each nest individually, map it to Slot or Tester instead. Tester and slot combinations are never pooled. No nested multi-appraiser model, attribute study, historical process sigma or confidence intervals. Zero total variation makes %Study Var N/A; zero Gage R&R makes NDC N/A. Results are statistical estimates subject to model, data quality and assumptions.
